instantiated_cells.justification: Section 13.66 prohibits any person from engaging in lobbying as a lobbyist unless licensed under §13.63, which requires application to and license issuance by the commission.
A lobbyist license issued under §13.63(1)(a) expires on December 31 of each even-numbered year, meaning a biennial (24-month) renewal cadence.

Lobbyists must be individually licensed under §13.63, principals must separately register under §13.64, and a separate written authorization must be filed under §13.65 for each principal-lobbyist relationship.
Section 13.63(1)(a) enumerates the application requirements (signature, SSN, fee) and does not require a photograph, and no other section in the subchapter imposes a photograph requirement.
Section 13.621(3) exempts elective state officials, local officials, tribal officials, and legislative employees from §§13.63, 13.64, 13.65, 13.68, and 13.695 when acting in an official capacity.

An agency that files a statement under §13.695 (and named officials) is exempt from §§13.625, 13.63, 13.64, 13.65, and 13.68 except as provided in §13.695, constituting a partial exemption with separate disclosure obligations.

unscoreable_emissions.reason: The statute requires principals to provide written notice before lobbying in a new area (§13.64(3)) and agencies to report changes within 10 days (§13.695(2)), but no specific deadline is set for a lobbyist to amend their own license/registration.

Wisconsin requires the lobbyist to be licensed BEFORE engaging in lobbying (§13.66 and §13.65 require licensing/authorization before lobbying), so there is no statutory "days after first lobbying" deadline for the lobbyist; the 10-day post-threshold deadline in §13.64(1) applies to the principal's registration, not the lobbyist's license.
